chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abu Ayyub al-Khazzaz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

A man asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and I was seated, about a man who had attained from his maternal aunt during his youth, then he restrained. Can he marry her daughter? He said: No. I said: He did not happen to have copulated with her; rather, it was something less than a thing. He said: His words are not accepted, and it is not honourable.
ai.seo_question: Can a man marry his mistress's daughter if he claims they only had partial relations?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes that a man who had illicit relations with a woman is barred from marrying her daughter, a ruling known as *al-Karamah* (or *al-Ladhdhah*) in Shia jurisprudence. Although the narrator interjects that the man claimed only partial intimacy occurred, the Imam rejects his testimony, emphasizing that the mere act of illicit connection creates a permanent impediment to marrying the daughter, regardless of the degree of penetration. This highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the credibility of the act itself over technical legal definitions of full consummation in determining marital prohibitions.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Abu Ayoub Al Khazzaz, from Muhammad Bin Muslim who said,

‘A man asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, and I was seated, about a man who had attained from his maternal aunt during his youth. Then he restrained. Can he marry her daughter?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No’. I said, ‘He did not happen to have copulated with her. But rather, something less than a thing’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No, his words are not accepted, and it is not honourable’.
en.sarwar: 10. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from abu Ayyub al-Khazzaz from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following: “

Once, a man asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, when I was sitting, about the case of a man who when young was involved with his maternal aunt then refrained, if he could marry her daughter. He (the Imam) said, ‘No, he cannot do so.’ He then asked, ‘What happens if there was no sexual intercourse, but it was something near the thing?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘No, his words are not accepted, and it is not honorable.’”
